issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path: there is no handling of load failures (EventType.LoadError is only mentioned in passing), a missing state machine or input name, or a null input, and no example of Data Binding despite recommending it.
Code and instructions are web and React only, even though the compatibility field lists Flutter, iOS, Android and React Native, and none of those platforms get any usage guidance.

scenarios.name: hover-icon-react-component
scenarios.rationale: Both responses use useRive and useStateMachineInput with 'IconStates' in stateMachines, set isHovered true on enter and false on leave with a null guard, and give the component an explicit size. B is slightly ahead because it names the collapse risk directly and mentions the webgl2 option, while A's configurable size prop and className are comparable.

scenarios.name: press-button-with-click-handler
scenarios.rationale: B puts the mouse handlers directly on RiveComponent, reads both inputs, resets isPressed on leave and on mouse up, calls onClick on mouse up, and sets an explicit 200x60 size. A uses pointer events instead of the mouse events the rubric names, sets the size on a wrapper div, and gates onClick behind a press-started check, so it only partly follows the rubric's mouse-up behavior.

scenarios.name: vanilla-player-with-events-and-cleanup
scenarios.rationale: A includes stateMachines, autoplay, EventType.RiveEvent, cleanup(), and the deprecation note (RiveEvent deprecated, autoBind, Load maintained), though it uses onLoad rather than rive.on(EventType.Load) in the code; B omits stateMachines from the code and has no deprecation note, though it has solid cleanup, off(), and event handling.
